However, the 2-column grid with consistent cards follows a standard marketplace pattern without distinctive visual language. Spacing inconsistencies in the bottom row slightly reduce precision.

observation.happening: Real-time meeting transcription with AI-powered categorization of conversation into semantic buckets (decisions, actions, questions, etc.)
observation.most_important: Split-pane design: left pane shows categorized conversation flow; right pane shows filtered view with speaker tags and timeline. Top bar shows recording state and audio waveform.
observation.next_action: Review categorized items, switch tabs to see different views (original/translation/live), or access AI resources
anomalies: Left and right panes display synchronized but differently-filtered data
Category-based organization is contextually intelligent rather than generic

4DA8.why: Sophisticated meeting intelligence platform with exceptional information hierarchy. The category system (決まったこと=decisions, やること=actions, 質問=questions) demonstrates thoughtful domain understanding rather than generic patterns. Time synchronization across panes, clear speaker identification, and dual-view system (raw + processed) show mature information design. State indicators (recording status, speaker badges) are precise. The only minor tension is high information density reducing visual calmness, but appropriate for context.

4EE8.why: Functional resource management modal with clear tab structure and well-executed progress bars. The authorization workflow is explicit. However, the sparse content within a narrow modal creates awkward proportions, and the tab/progress pattern is a standard integration UX without distinctive approach. The modal itself interrupts the meeting flow appropriately but offers no novel interaction model.

observation.happening: Meeting interface in degraded state: voice recognition permission denied, transcription halted, but audio recording continues
observation.most_important: Error/warning state with peach-colored banner at top, red-text sidebar warning, and empty transcript area. User is explicitly guided toward resolution (settings button).
observation.next_action: Click 'Open settings' button to grant voice recognition permission
anomalies: Three layers of error messaging (banner + sidebar + footer) creates redundancy
Large empty whitespace in transcript pane makes interface feel broken
Stark contrast between detailed error messaging and empty content suggests unfinished state

ai_look: repetitive error messaging across multiple layers
large empty space with minimal content
53CB.why: While the error state is unmistakably clear and the banner button is well-designed, the overall interface feels unpolished. The triple-layer messaging (peach banner + red sidebar text + footer note) is redundant and creates tension rather than calm. The vast empty transcript area with only error text makes the interface appear broken rather than gracefully degraded. A production interface should either show placeholder content (silence indicator, time elapsed) or use more restrained error messaging to maintain visual balance.

observation.happening: Compact dark control bar for Google Meet showing meeting status and action buttons
observation.most_important: Time display (05:12), functional buttons (memo/subtitles/Ask Astra/pause/record), recording indicator as red circle
observation.next_action: Click action buttons or use recording/pause controls
anomalies: Seven interface elements compressed into pill-shaped bar creates dense information arrangement
No visual hierarchy among action buttons—all equal prominence

5475.why: Well-executed compact control bar with high information density and polished appearance. The dark background is appropriately unobtrusive for video meeting context, and the recording state is clear via red circle. Icon selection is thoughtful. However, all buttons have equal visual weight creating no action priority hierarchy, and the pill-shaped bar design is a standard Google/Apple meeting UI pattern without distinction.
